items.title: Building an AI Agent With LangGraph and Python
items.description: Learn LangGraph in Python with this hands-on video course and build a stateful AI agent using state graphs, nodes, and conditional edges.
items.summary: LangGraph is a versatile Python framework designed for stateful, cyclic, and multi-actor Large Language Model (LLM) applications. LangGraph builds on its parent library, LangChain, and allows you to build sophisticated workflows that can handle the complexities of real-world LLM applications.

items.title: How to Round Numbers in Python
items.description: Learn how Python's round() works, why it rounds 2.5 to 2, and how you can manage rounding errors with decimal, NumPy, and pandas.
items.summary: Rounding numbers in Python is an essential task, especially when dealing with data precision. Python’s built-in round() function uses the rounding half to even strategy, which rounds numbers like 2.5 to 2 and 3.5 to 4 .

items.title: Asynchronous Tasks With Django and Celery
items.description: Integrate Django and Celery with Redis as a message broker, and move slow work like sending email out of the request cycle.
items.summary: Celery is a distributed task queue that processes tasks asynchronously, so slow work doesn’t hold up your web app’s response. When you integrate Celery with your Django application, you can offload time-consuming tasks and keep your users from waiting.

items.title: Digging Deeper Into Django Migrations
items.description: Go beyond the basics of Django migrations: how they work under the hood, what the Django migrations table tracks, and what's inside migration files.
items.summary: You already understand the purpose of Django migrations and you’re familiar with fundamental usage patterns like creating and applying migrations. In this tutorial, you’ll dig deeper into the migration system and take a peek at some of its underlying mechanics, from the Django migrations table to the migration files themselves.

items.title: Python's Mutable vs Immutable Types: What's the Difference?
items.description: Learn how Python mutable and immutable data types work internally and how you can use mutability or immutability to power your code.
items.summary: Python’s mutable objects, such as lists and dictionaries, allow you to change their value or data directly without affecting their identity. In contrast, immutable objects, like tuples and strings, don’t allow in-place modifications.

items.title: Django Migrations: A Primer
items.description: Get comfortable with Django migrations: create database tables without writing SQL, and keep your database in step as your models change.
items.summary: Since version 1.7, Django has come with built-in support for database migrations. In Django , database migrations usually go hand in hand with models: whenever you code up a new model, you also generate a migration to create the necessary table in the database.

items.description: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which…
items.summary: We present EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model which natively represents text, images, audio, video, and combinations thereof in a unified space. Our approach introduces improvements such as simplified per-layer embeddings and a multi-stage curriculum with modality and objective progression which ensure strong quality across unimodal, cross-modal, and mixed-modal evaluations.

items.title: Python's Instance, Class, and Static Methods Demystified

items.summary: Instance, class, and static methods each serve a distinct role in Python, and knowing when to use one over another is key to writing clean, maintainable code. Instance methods operate on individual objects using self , while class methods use cls to access class-level data.
